title: GaleOps telemetry partnership angles
body:
Notes to self — quick scratchpad for GaleOps (observability vendor) outreach and pilot pitch

Background / why GaleOps might care
- GaleOps sells lightweight ML telemetry + anomaly detection for model inference pipelines. Focus on low-overhead agents, multi-cloud ingestion, and schema-driven dashboards.
- Possible overlap with Redwood: we provide inference runtime + placement; they provide instrumentation/alerting. Partnership could be: native instrumentation hooks from Redwood runtime -> GaleOps pipeline (reduces customer integration friction), co-sell pilot to mid-market fintechs.

Account research highlights (from website + quick LinkedIn sweep)
- HQ: SF. ~120 employees. Recent Series B (2024) per TechCrunch note.
- CTO: Priya Narang — background in infra monitoring (previously at NimbusOps).
- Head of Partnerships: Tom Reed — recent hire from a cloud vendor.
- Product lead for SDKs: Arun Mehta — likely owner for integration conversations.
- Existing customers: 4 retail/fintech case studies showing inferencing telemetry (mentions 'low agent overhead' and 'edge-friendly').
- Recent blog: "Observability for inference at scale" (Oct 2025) — mentions custom KV cache telemetry. Good signal: they understand LLM inference-specific telemetry.

Technical fit / integration ideas
- Endpoints: offer a Redwood side plugin that emits structured events (request_id, model, model_variant, seq_len, batched_size, kv_cache_hit, latency_ms, gpu_pci_util, quant_profile).
- Two integration flavors:
  1) Hosted hook: webhook/HTTP sink from Redwood hosted plane -> GaleOps ingest (fast to demo).
  2) Private connector: small sidecar (gRPC) for Redwood Private customers to stream telemetry into customer-managed GaleOps instance (compliant setups).
- Value props for GaleOps to co-sell:
  - Immediate observability for inference KPIs (per-model token latency, cache hit rate)
  - Alerting on model regressions (drift detection tied to prompt templates)
  - Customer stickiness: combined bills + config reduces chance of churn.

Who to reach / intro plan
- Primary: Tom Reed (Head of Partnerships) — outreach to evaluate interest in co-marketing and a pilot.
- Secondary: Arun Mehta (SDK/product) — technical alignment for minimal integration surface.
- Warm path: find who at Redwood knows Tom — check internal CRM/LinkedIn (Diego said he has 2nd-degree).

Outbound messaging (cold -> warm) 
- Subject line ideas:
  1) "Redwood + GaleOps: quick idea for inference telemetry pilots"
  2) "Lower friction inference observability — pilot proposal"
  3) "Idea: native telemetry hook for LLM inference (short pilot)"

- Cold email (short):
  Hi Tom —

  I’m Aisha on the partnerships team at Redwood (we run a production inference platform used by a lot of fintechs/marketplaces). Noticed GaleOps’ work on inference observability — curious whether you’ve explored native telemetry hooks from runtimes (request-level model metrics + KV cache signals).

  We think a short pilot (2–4 weeks) to stream a subset of metrics from Redwood -> GaleOps could show clear lead-gen and integration value. No infra changes for customers in hosted mode; private connector option for enterprise.

  Would you be open to a 20-minute call next week to sketch a pilot?

  Best,
  Aisha

- Follow-up sequence (2 short touches + LinkedIn):
  1) If no reply in 5 days — add a concrete signal ("we've seen 15% token cost reduction for customers who enable KV cache metrics")
  2) If no reply in 10 days — offer a joint customer intro (pilot candidate) or a quick tech sync with Arun.

Meeting agenda (20 min pilot sync)
- 5m intros + alignment on goals
- 7m integration surface (webhook vs sidecar) + data schema (show sample payload)
- 5m pilot success metrics (time-to-value, alerts created, demo dashboard)
- 3m next steps / timeline

Pilot scope (1 pager sketch)
- Duration: 3 weeks (dev + 1 week validation)
- Success metrics:
  - Instrumentation: payload up to 10k events/day for small pilot customer
  - Visibility: dashboard showing latency distribution, cache-hit rate, queue depth within 1 day of integration
  - Actionability: at least one alert or anomaly detected that results in a config change or rollback during pilot
- Deliverables: Redwood plugin (hosted webhook), simple GaleOps dashboard template, joint case study outline

Common objections + short scripts
- "We already have telemetry for infra" -> "Yes — infra telemetry is helpful, but inference telemetry (per-request model metrics, kv cache hits, token-level latencies) is different; it directly ties to model economics and RLHF/regression signals. We can send only the inference slice so you don't duplicate infra noise."
- "Security/PII concerns" -> "We can strip or hash any text fields; telemetry payload can be schema-only: no prompts, only hashes and token counts. For private deployments, sidecar option keeps data in-customer VPC."
- "Integration overhead / SDK work" -> "Host hook approach is zero-customer-change for hosted mode; for Private, the sidecar is a single small binary we can provide with a clear config + tests. Offer dev support for first pilot customer."
- "Why Redwood vs direct agent?" -> "We control the serving runtime and can emit richer signals (batch composition, KV cache hits, model variant rollouts) that product SDKs don't surface consistently across vendors."

Pricing / commercial angle (high level)
- Start with co-marketing + free pilot.
- After pilot: revenue share on joint customers or referral commission; alternative: an integration listing fee + lead credits. Need to get finance input if we talk formal revenue split.

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] Ask Diego to intros Tom (Diego has 2nd-degree).
- [ ] Draft short tech payload (sample JSON) for Arun to review — include request_id, model_name, seq_len, batch_size, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), quant_profile. (Arun will want simple schema).
- [ ] Find 1 candidate Redwood customer that uses both hosted API and has compliance tolerance for pilot (preferably non-SOE).
- [ ] Get legal draft for minimal DPA addendum for telemetry sharing (sales-sourcing).
- [ ] Prep a 10-slide co-demo deck (I can reuse parts of partner-ops template).

Quick prototype sample payload (for notes) — remove before sharing publicly:
{ request_id: "r-123", ts: 1700000000, model: "redwood-7b-v2", variant: "q4_0", seq_len: 64, batch_size: 8, latency_ms: 45, kv_cache_hit: true, gpu_util: 62.1 }

Slack cues / internal handoffs
- Post pilot interest -> #partners for co-marketing resources, cc Maya for case-study copy.
- Engineering sync -> create ticket JIRA-ENG-1428 (linked above).

Rough heuristics to call out in conversation (short bullets to memorize)
- Typical token-level latency range: 20–200ms depending on model & quantization
- Prefix/KV cache hits reduce token generation latency significantly — customers often don't surface this metric to observability teams
- A 5–10% change in per-request batching or cache-hit rate can swing monthly inference spend noticeably for heavy users

Personal notes (meta)
- Keep first outreach lightweight. Tom is partnerships head — emphasise co-selling + low lift.
- If Tom pushes to product, loop Arun early. Don't ask for legal until technical interest is confirmed.

Last edited: quick checklist before outreach
- [ ] Payload example ready
- [ ] Short email template + 1 follow-up ready
- [ ] Diego intro request queued
- [ ] Internal partner channels primed (marketing + engineering)

End of scratchpad.
